properties.name: Roee Ozeri
properties.short_bio: Prof. Roee Ozeri is an experimental physicist working in atomic physics and quantum information science. He earned a BSc in Physics from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and completed his MSc and PhD in Physics at the Weizmann Institute of Science under Prof. Nir Davidson, focusing on optical manipulation of atomic clouds.

properties.name: Ziv Meir
properties.short_bio: Dr. Ziv Meir is an experimental physicist and principal investigator at the Weizmann Institute of Science. His research develops quantum-logic techniques originally created for trapped-ion quantum computing and optical clocks to control, detect, and manipulate single trapped molecular ions, enabling molecular qubits and new precision spectroscopy capabilities.

properties.name: Chris Ballance
properties.short_bio: Dr. Chris Ballance is a physicist and quantum-technology leader working on trapped-ion quantum computing across academia and industry. He completed his DPhil (PhD) at the University of Oxford under Prof. David M. Lucas, with a thesis on high-fidelity trapped-ion quantum logic.

properties.name: Christopher R. Monroe

current_position.title: Gilhuly Family Presidential Distinguished Professor; Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering and Physics

properties.short_bio: Christopher R. Monroe is a physicist and a leading figure in trapped-ion quantum information science. He is the Gilhuly Family Presidential Distinguished Professor of Electrical & Computer Engineering and Physics at Duke University, and a co-founder of IonQ, a company commercializing trapped-ion quantum computers.

properties.name: Christian F. Roos
properties.short_bio: Dr. Christian F. Roos is an experimental physicist working on trapped-ion quantum science, including quantum simulation and precision spectroscopy. He is affiliated with IQOQI Innsbruck (Austrian Academy of Sciences) and the University of Innsbruck.

properties.name: David J. Wineland

current_position.title: Philip H. Knight Distinguished Research Chair; Research Professor (Physics)

properties.short_bio: David J. Wineland is a Nobel Prize–winning experimental physicist known for pioneering techniques to **trap, laser-cool, and coherently control single ions**, enabling major advances in **precision atomic clocks** and **trapped-ion quantum information processing**. He spent decades at NIST (Boulder) building the historic Ion Storage Group, where his laboratory developed foundational methods for high-fidelity quantum logic with ions and optical clocks using Aluminum and Mercury ions. In 2018, he joined the University of Oregon as a Research Professor.

properties.name: Dietrich Leibfried

current_position.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Boulder
current_position.title: Staff Physicist / Co-Leader, Ion Storage Group (Quantum Information)

properties.short_bio: Dietrich Leibfried is a leading experimental physicist in trapped-ion quantum information science at NIST (Boulder). He received his PhD (Dr. rer. nat., summa cum laude) from Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München in 1995 under Theodor W. Hänsch, working on precision laser spectroscopy of hydrogen at the Max Planck Institute for Quantum Optics.

properties.name: John J. Bollinger

current_position.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Boulder
current_position.title: Staff Scientist / Group Leader, Ion Storage Group

properties.short_bio: John J. Bollinger is a staff scientist and current group leader of the NIST Ion Storage Group in the Time and Frequency Division. He received undergraduate degrees in physics and mathematics from Cornell University (1974) and a PhD in physics from Harvard University (1981) under Arthur Pipkin.

properties.name: Hartmut Häffner
properties.short_bio: Hartmut Häffner is a professor of physics at UC Berkeley and affiliated with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, leading The Ion Trap Group focused on trapped-ion quantum science.

properties.name: Jungsang Kim

current_position.title: Schiciano Family Distinguished Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering; Professor of Physics

properties.short_bio: Jungsang Kim leads the Multifunctional Integrated Systems Technology (MIST) group at Duke University. He is the Schiciano Family Distinguished Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering and Professor of Physics, and serves as Associate Director of the Duke Quantum Center.

properties.name: Kihwan Kim

current_position.institution: Institute for Basic Science (IBS), South Korea
current_position.title: Director, Center for Trapped Ion Quantum Science

properties.short_bio: Kihwan Kim is a leading trapped-ion quantum computing experimentalist and Director of the Center for Trapped Ion Quantum Science at the Institute for Basic Science (IBS) in South Korea, a position he assumed in late 2025.

properties.name: Winfried K. Hensinger

current_position.title: Professor of Quantum Technologies; Director, Sussex Centre for Quantum Technologies

properties.short_bio: Winfried K. Hensinger is a Professor of Quantum Technologies at the University of Sussex, where he leads the Sussex Ion Quantum Technology Group and directs the Sussex Centre for Quantum Technologies. He is also the Co-founder, Chief Scientist, and Chairman of Universal Quantum, a full-stack quantum computing company spun out of his lab in 2018.

properties.name: Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler
properties.short_bio: Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler is a Full Professor of Experimental Physics at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, where he leads the "Quantenbit AG" research group, and is a member of the Helmholtz Institute Mainz.

properties.name: Thomas Monz
properties.short_bio: Thomas Monz is an experimental quantum physicist serving as a Senior Scientist at the University of Innsbruck and is the Co-founder and CEO of Alpine Quantum Technologies (AQT), an Austrian spin-out developing general-purpose trapped-ion quantum computers.

properties.name: Tracy E. Northup
properties.short_bio: Tracy E. Northup is a Full Professor of Experimental Physics at the University of Innsbruck, where she leads the Quantum Interfaces group. Her research pioneers the integration of trapped ions with optical cavities to create robust light-matter interfaces for quantum networking, communication, and sensing. She also explores hybrid optomechanical systems, including trapping nanoparticles in ion traps.

properties.name: Jonathan P. Home
properties.short_bio: Jonathan P. Home is a Full Professor of Physics at ETH Zürich, where he leads the Trapped Ion Quantum Information (TIQI) group. His research focuses on precision control, error correction, and scalable architectures for trapped-ion quantum computing, including integrated trap technologies with photonic components.

properties.name: Rainer Blatt

current_position.institution: Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information (IQOQI) Innsbruck
current_position.title: Emeritus Research Director

properties.short_bio: Rainer Blatt is an experimental physicist who helped establish **trapped ions** as a leading platform for **quantum information processing**, **quantum simulation**, and **precision measurement**. He is a Professor at the University of Innsbruck and an Emeritus Research Director at IQOQI Innsbruck (ÖAW), and he is a co-founder of Alpine Quantum Technologies (AQT), a trapped-ion quantum computing company spun out from his research at Innsbruck.

properties.name: Michael Drewsen
properties.short_bio: Michael Drewsen is a professor at Aarhus University and leads research in trapped-ion physics, with particular focus on molecular ions, large Coulomb crystals, and quantum simulation. His group has made significant contributions to sympathetic cooling techniques and precision spectroscopy of molecular ions, and he authored early seminal work on forming large ion crystals in linear Paul traps.

properties.name: Michael Köhl
properties.short_bio: Michael Köhl is a professor at the University of Bonn leading research in experimental quantum physics with trapped ions and ultracold atomic gases. His group focuses on quantum communication nodes using trapped ytterbium ions coupled to optical cavities, developing quantum networks, and exploring quantum information processing with fiber-based systems.

properties.name: Luming Duan

current_position.title: Yao Qizhi Chair Professor / Chair Professor of Basic Sciences

properties.short_bio: Luming Duan is the Yao Qizhi Chair Professor at Tsinghua University's Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences (IIIS), an Academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (2023), and a Principal Investigator at the Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute.

properties.name: Michael J. Biercuk

current_position.title: Professor of Quantum Physics; Director, Quantum Control Laboratory

properties.short_bio: Michael J. Biercuk is a Professor of Quantum Physics and Director of the Quantum Control Laboratory at the University of Sydney. He is also the founder and CEO of Q-CTRL, a leading quantum technology company specializing in quantum infrastructure software and error suppression.

properties.name: K. Rajibul Islam

current_position.institution: Institute for Quantum Computing, University of Waterloo
current_position.title: Associate Professor

properties.short_bio: K. Rajibul Islam is an Associate Professor at the Institute for Quantum Computing (IQC) and the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Waterloo. His research focuses on experimental quantum many-body physics, particularly the quantum simulation of frustrated spin models with trapped ions. He leads the Laboratory for Quantum Information with Trapped Ions (QITI), which is developing "QuantumIon", a multi-user, open-access trapped-ion quantum computer. He also co-founded Open Quantum Design, a non-profit foundation developing open-source, full-stack trapped-ion quantum computing blueprints.

properties.name: Crystal Senko

current_position.institution: Institute for Quantum Computing, University of Waterloo
current_position.title: Associate Professor / Canada Research Chair in Trapped Ion Quantum Computing

properties.short_bio: Crystal Senko is an Associate Professor at the Institute for Quantum Computing (IQC) at the University of Waterloo, and the Canada Research Chair in Trapped Ion Quantum Computing. Her research focuses on trapped-ion quantum simulation and computing, particularly utilizing multi-level qudits in barium ions. She co-founded Open Quantum Design to create the world's first open-source, full-stack trapped-ion quantum computer.

properties.name: Paul Haljan
properties.short_bio: Paul Haljan is an Associate Professor of Physics at Simon Fraser University, where he leads the Trapped Ion Quantum Technology Lab. His research focuses on trapped-ion quantum technologies, including scalable quantum computing with cadmium and ytterbium ions, microstructure development for ion trap designs, and high-fidelity entanglement operations.

properties.name: Christian Schmiegelow
properties.short_bio: Christian Schmiegelow leads the Laboratory of Cold Ions and Atoms at the University of Buenos Aires, Argentina. His research focuses on trapped-ion quantum optics, particularly the interaction of ions with structured light (like optical orbital angular momentum), and quantum information processing. His lab represents a key center for experimental ion trapping research in South America.

properties.name: Erik W. Streed

current_position.title: Associate Professor; Director, Queensland Quantum and Advanced Technologies Research Institute

properties.short_bio: Erik W. Streed is an Associate Professor at Griffith University and Director of the Queensland Quantum and Advanced Technologies Research Institute. His research uniquely bridges quantum physics and biology, applying trapped-ion techniques to biomolecular dynamics, advanced single-atom imaging, and quantum computing.

properties.name: Lukáš Slodička
properties.short_bio: Lukáš Slodička leads the Trapped Ions group in the Department of Optics at Palacký University Olomouc, Czech Republic. His research focuses on quantum optics with trapped ions, particularly atom-light interactions and efficient ion-photon interfaces for quantum networking.

properties.name: Jürgen Eschner
properties.short_bio: Jürgen Eschner leads the Quantum Photonics Group at Saarland University, where the research program is dedicated to the controlled interaction between light and matter in the quantum mechanical regime. The main objective of his group’s work is to study and experimentally realize the transformation between quantum states of individual photons and individual atoms/ions, employing high-finesse optical resonators, single trapped particles, and entangled photon pairs.

properties.name: Christof Wunderlich
properties.short_bio: Christof Wunderlich leads the Quantum Optics Research Group at the University of Siegen. His group is known for pioneering work on microwave-driven quantum logic with trapped ytterbium ions and magnetic gradient traps (MAGIC) for scalable quantum information processing. He is also a co-founder of the quantum computing startup eleQtron.

properties.name: Rene Gerritsma
properties.short_bio: Rene Gerritsma leads research on Hybrid Atom-Ion Quantum Systems at the University of Amsterdam. His group explores the interface between ultracold neutral atoms and trapped ions for quantum simulation and quantum information applications.

properties.name: Jeroen C. J. Koelemeij
properties.short_bio: Jeroen C. J. Koelemeij leads the HD+ spectroscopy team at VU Amsterdam. His research focuses on precision spectroscopy of molecular hydrogen ions (HD+) for tests of fundamental physics and determination of fundamental constants.

properties.name: Murray D. Barrett

current_position.institution: Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore
current_position.title: Principal Investigator

properties.short_bio: Murray D. Barrett is a Principal Investigator at the Centre for Quantum Technologies (CQT) at the National University of Singapore, where he leads the Microtraps Group. His research focuses on developing microfabricated ion traps for scalable quantum computing and quantum networking with barium and lutetium ions.

properties.name: Dzmitry Matsukevich

current_position.institution: Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore
current_position.title: Principal Investigator

properties.short_bio: Dzmitry Matsukevich is a Principal Investigator at the Centre for Quantum Technologies (CQT) at the National University of Singapore. His group focuses on trapped ion quantum information processing, quantum thermodynamics, and utilizing trapped molecular ions (such as SiO+) for quantum networking and precision measurements.

properties.name: Manas Mukherjee

current_position.institution: Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore
current_position.title: Principal Investigator

properties.short_bio: Manas Mukherjee leads the Cold Ion Group at the Centre for Quantum Technologies (CQT) in Singapore. His research focuses on trapped-ion quantum computing, quantum simulation, and precision measurement with barium ions.

properties.name: Stefan Willitsch
properties.short_bio: Stefan Willitsch is a Professor of Chemistry at the University of Basel, where he leads a research group focused on trapped molecular ions, cold ion-molecule reactions, and quantum chemistry at ultracold temperatures. His group has made landmark contributions to controlling and probing chemical reactions at the quantum level using hybrid ion-atom traps.

properties.name: Richard C. Thompson
properties.short_bio: Richard C. Thompson is a Professor of Experimental Physics at Imperial College London, where he leads the Ion Trapping Group within the Quantum Optics and Laser Science (QOLS) section. His group has been a long-established center for trapped-ion quantum information research, working with calcium ions on quantum computing and fundamental ion trap technology.

properties.name: David M. Lucas
properties.short_bio: David M. Lucas is the Hooke Professor of Experimental Physics at the University of Oxford, where he co-leads the Oxford Ion Trap Quantum Computing Group. The Oxford group is one of the world's leading centers for trapped-ion quantum computing, working with calcium and strontium ions on quantum error correction, high-fidelity quantum gates, and optical clocks.

properties.name: Eric R. Hudson
properties.short_bio: Eric R. Hudson leads the Hudson Lab at UCLA, focusing on trapped molecular ions, ultracold chemistry, and quantum simulation. His group works with barium, ytterbium, and molecular ions to explore ion-neutral collisions and chemical reactions at ultracold temperatures.

properties.name: Wesley C. Campbell
properties.short_bio: Wesley C. Campbell leads the Campbell Lab at UCLA, focusing on trapped-ion quantum simulation and quantum computing with ytterbium ions. His research also includes precision measurement and optical atomic clocks.

properties.name: Vladan Vuletić
properties.short_bio: Vladan Vuletić is the Lester Wolfe Professor of Physics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). His experimental research focuses on ultracold atoms, quantum optics, many-body quantum entanglement, cavity QED, and quantum information processing. While primarily known for his pioneering work with neutral atoms, he has also made significant contributions to trapped-ion cavity QED interfaces.

properties.name: Isaac L. Chuang

current_position.title: Professor of Physics and Electrical Engineering; Senior Associate Dean of Digital Learning

properties.short_bio: Isaac L. Chuang is a Professor of Physics and Professor of Electrical Engineering at MIT, where he leads the Quanta Group within the Center for Ultracold Atoms. He also serves as the Senior Associate Dean of Digital Learning.

properties.name: Kenneth R. Brown

current_position.title: Michael J. Fitzpatrick Distinguished Professor of Engineering; Director of the Duke Quantum Center

properties.short_bio: Kenneth R. Brown is the Michael J. Fitzpatrick Distinguished Professor of Engineering at Duke University and the Director of the Duke Quantum Center. He holds appointments in the Departments of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Physics, and Chemistry.

properties.name: Kilian Singer
properties.short_bio: Kilian Singer leads the Trapped Ion Quantum Information and Thermodynamics group at the University of Kassel. His research focuses on single-ion heat engines, thermodynamics in the quantum regime, and scalable ion trap technologies using calcium ions.

properties.name: Johannes Hecker Denschlag

current_position.title: Professor; Head of the Institute of Quantum Matter

properties.short_bio: Johannes Hecker Denschlag is a Professor of Physics and Head of the Institute of Quantum Matter at Ulm University. His group investigates ultracold quantum gases and pioneering hybrid systems of trapped ions immersed in neutral atom clouds, focusing on cold ion-atom collisions and quantum chemistry.

properties.name: Kazuhiro Hayasaka

current_position.institution: National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT)
current_position.title: Group Leader

properties.short_bio: Kazuhiro Hayasaka leads the Space-Time Standards Laboratory at NICT in Kobe, Japan. His research focuses on developing high-precision optical clocks using trapped indium and calcium ions for frequency standards and metrology. He was also a co-author on early seminal work demonstrating continuous single-photon generation in an ion-trap cavity system.

properties.name: Kjeld S. E. Eikema
properties.short_bio: Kjeld S. E. Eikema leads the Ultrafast Laser Physics and Precision Metrology group at VU Amsterdam and is a Group Leader at the Advanced Research Center for Nanolithography (ARCNL). His research combines frequency combs with trapped ions and neutral atoms (such as helium) for extreme precision measurements and tests of fundamental physics and Quantum Electrodynamics (QED).

properties.name: Klaus Jungmann
properties.short_bio: Klaus Jungmann leads the Fundamental Interactions and Symmetries group at the University of Groningen. His prominent work involves precision measurements with trapped radium and barium ions to test fundamental symmetries and search for physics beyond the Standard Model.

properties.name: Hermann Uys
properties.short_bio: Hermann Uys leads the trapped ion research group at Stellenbosch University and the CSIR in South Africa. His work focuses on trapped ytterbium ions for quantum control, simulation of many-body physics, and quantum thermodynamics.

properties.name: Patrick Gill
properties.short_bio: Patrick Gill is a Senior NPL Fellow and Fellow of the Royal Society, specializing in optical frequency standards and trapped-ion optical clocks at the National Physical Laboratory (NPL) in the UK. He is a world-leading pioneer in high-precision metrology, particularly using strontium and ytterbium ions. His landmark 2004 Science paper achieved hertz-level measurements of the optical clock frequency in a single 88Sr+ ion.

properties.name: Rachel Godun
properties.short_bio: Rachel Godun is a Principal Scientist at the National Physical Laboratory (NPL), where she leads the Ytterbium Ion Optical Clock team. Her research focuses on developing and improving trapped-ion optical clocks for next-generation timekeeping and fundamental physics tests, including constraints on the time variation of fundamental constants.

properties.name: John Chiaverini
properties.short_bio: John Chiaverini leads trapped-ion research at MIT Lincoln Laboratory. His work focuses on scalable quantum computing architectures, integrated photonics for ion traps, and surface-electrode trap technology.

properties.name: Dan Stick
properties.short_bio: Dan Stick leads the trapped ion trap fabrication and testing efforts at Sandia National Laboratories. His High Optical Access (HOA) surface traps are widely used in the community, and his research focuses on integrating optics and improving trap technologies for quantum computing.

properties.name: Masao Kitano
properties.short_bio: Masao Kitano leads research in quantum optics and trapped-ion systems at Kyoto University. His work focuses on quantum information processing with ytterbium ions.

properties.name: Hiroki Takahashi

current_position.institution: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST)
current_position.title: Associate Professor

properties.short_bio: Hiroki Takahashi is an Associate Professor at OIST, where he leads the Experimental Quantum Information Physics Unit. His research focuses on trapped-ion quantum networks and cavity QED with calcium and barium ions.

properties.name: Takashi Mukaiyama
properties.short_bio: Takashi Mukaiyama is a Professor at Osaka University. His research group focuses on trapped-ion quantum logic spectroscopy, optical clock development, and precision measurements using calcium and indium ions.

properties.name: Kenji Toyoda
properties.short_bio: Kenji Toyoda conducts trapped-ion research at Osaka University, focusing on quantum simulation, quantum computing, and motional phonon dynamics with calcium ions.

properties.name: Utako Tanaka
properties.short_bio: Utako Tanaka is an Associate Professor at Osaka University. Her research group focuses on the design, fabrication, and operation of microfabricated surface-electrode ion traps, primarily using calcium ions for quantum computing and quantum simulation applications. She is a key participant in the international TRiAC collaboration for advanced trap development.

properties.name: Atsushi Noguchi
properties.short_bio: Atsushi Noguchi is an Associate Professor at the University of Tokyo, where he leads research on hybrid quantum systems combining trapped ions (specifically beryllium) with superconducting circuits.

properties.name: Shuichi Hasegawa
properties.short_bio: Shuichi Hasegawa leads trapped-ion research at the University of Tokyo focusing on laser cooling and quantum control with calcium ions.

properties.name: Moonjoo Lee
properties.short_bio: Moonjoo Lee leads the trapped-ion quantum computing group at POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology). His research focuses on quantum simulation, quantum computing, and cavity QED with ytterbium ions.

properties.name: Taeyoung Choi
properties.short_bio: Taeyoung Choi leads trapped-ion research at Ewha Womans University in Seoul, focusing on quantum computing and quantum control with ytterbium ions.

properties.name: Dan Cho
properties.short_bio: Dong-il "Dan" Cho is a Professor at Seoul National University. His research group focuses on the engineering and microfabrication aspects of ion traps, specializing in MEMS technology to create scalable surface-electrode traps for quantum information processing with ytterbium ions.

properties.name: Taehyun Kim
properties.short_bio: Taehyun Kim is an Associate Professor at Seoul National University, where he leads the Quantum Information Systems Laboratory. His research focuses on trapped-ion quantum computing and quantum networks, particularly utilizing microfabricated surface traps and ytterbium ions.

properties.name: Junki Kim
properties.short_bio: Junki Kim is an Assistant Professor at Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU), where he leads the Quantum Engineering with Trapped Ions (QuETI) lab. His research focuses on trapped-ion quantum computing and simulation with ytterbium and barium ions, particularly architecting scalable quantum computers with ion shuttling.

properties.name: Luyan Sun
properties.short_bio: Luyan Sun leads quantum information research at Tsinghua University focusing on hybrid quantum systems and trapped-ion quantum computing.

properties.name: Wenhui Li
properties.short_bio: Wenhui Li is a Professor at Peking University, where she leads research on trapped ions and Rydberg atoms for quantum simulation and computing. Her research bridges two major platforms — cold Rydberg atomic ensembles and trapped-ion crystals — exploring their applications in quantum simulation.

properties.name: Mirko Lobino
properties.short_bio: Mirko Lobino leads quantum photonics and trapped-ion research at Griffith University in Brisbane, Australia, focusing on hybrid quantum systems and interfacing single trapped ions with quantum photonic circuits.

properties.name: Paul Barclay
properties.short_bio: Paul Barclay leads a quantum photonics research group at the University of Calgary focusing on hybrid quantum systems, diamond-based quantum technologies, and nanophotonics. His work explores coupling trapped ions and solid-state defects (like NV centers) to nanophotonic cavities for enhanced light-matter interaction.

properties.name: S. A. Rangwala
properties.short_bio: S. A. Rangwala is a Senior Professor leading cold atoms and ions research at the Raman Research Institute, focusing on hybrid ion-atom systems and cold collisions.

properties.name: Markus Hennrich
properties.short_bio: Markus Hennrich leads the Trapped Rydberg Ion Group at Stockholm University, pioneering work on Rydberg excitation of trapped ions (such as strontium) for fast quantum computing operations and quantum simulation.

properties.name: Matthias Keller
properties.short_bio: Matthias Keller leads trapped-ion research at the University of Sussex focusing on ion-photon interfaces and cavity QED for quantum networks.

properties.name: Brian McMahon
properties.short_bio: Brian McMahon is a Research Scientist at the Georgia Tech Research Institute (GTRI), leading trapped-ion research focused on quantum computing and quantum networks. His work has involved the development of compact, reconfigurable Penning ion traps and advanced Doppler cooling techniques for quantum simulation.

properties.name: David Hume

current_position.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Boulder
current_position.title: Physicist

properties.short_bio: David Hume leads the Aluminum Ion Clock project at NIST Boulder, developing the world's most precise optical atomic clocks using quantum logic spectroscopy.

properties.name: Piet O. Schmidt
properties.short_bio: Piet O. Schmidt leads the QUEST Institute for Experimental Quantum Metrology at PTB and Leibniz University Hannover. His research group is renowned for developing ultra-precise optical atomic clocks using trapped ions. He is a pioneer of quantum logic spectroscopy, a technique he co-developed during his postdoc, which allows the spectroscopy of ions that lack suitable transitions for direct laser cooling and detection (such as aluminum and highly charged ions).

properties.name: Boris B. Blinov
properties.short_bio: Boris B. Blinov leads the Trapped Ion Quantum Computing group at the University of Washington, focusing on barium ion quantum networks and ion-photon entanglement. His early seminal work included the first observation of entanglement between a single trapped atom and a single photon.

properties.name: Tilman Esslinger
properties.short_bio: Tilman Esslinger is a Professor of Physics at ETH Zürich, where he leads the Quantum Optics Group. His group is renowned for pioneering experiments with ultracold quantum gases in optical lattices and cavities, and more recently for hybrid atom-ion systems.

properties.name: Ben P. Lanyon
properties.short_bio: Ben P. Lanyon leads the Distributed Quantum Systems group at the University of Innsbruck, demonstrating long-distance entanglement distribution with trapped calcium ions and quantum networking protocols. He was also the lead author on a seminal 2011 paper demonstrating universal digital quantum simulation with trapped ions.

properties.name: Yuval Shagam

current_position.institution: Technion ג€“ Israel Institute of Technology
current_position.title: Assistant Professor

properties.short_bio: Prof. Yuval Shagam is an experimental physicist and Assistant Professor at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, where he leads the **Molecular Quantum Technology Lab**. His research centers on **precision molecular ion trapping**, **quantum control of molecular systems**, cold quantum chemistry, and **precision spectroscopy** for tests of fundamental symmetry (such as parity violation) and searches for physics beyond the Standard Model.

properties.name: Daniel Rodríguez Rubiales

current_position.title: Catedrático de Universidad (Full Professor of Physics)

properties.short_bio: Prof. **Daniel Rodríguez Rubiales** is a Spanish experimental physicist and *Catedrático de Universidad* at the **University of Granada**, where he leads the **Ion Traps and Lasers Laboratory** — Spain’s *only* experimental ion-trapping facility of its kind.

current_position.title: Joshua and Beth Friedman University Professor of Physics

properties.name: Immanuel Bloch
properties.short_bio: Immanuel Bloch is Professor of Experimental Physics at Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU) and Scientific Director of the Quantum Many-Body Systems Division at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics (MPQ) in Garching, where he has been based since 2008. He is one of the most cited physicists in quantum simulation, widely recognised for pioneering the use of optical lattices and quantum gas microscopes to realise and probe strongly correlated quantum systems with single-atom precision.

current_position.institution: JILA, University of Colorado Boulder / NIST
current_position.title: JILA and NIST Fellow; Professor Adjoint of Physics, University of Colorado Boulder

properties.name: Markus Greiner

current_position.title: George Vasmer Leverett Professor of Physics

properties.short_bio: Markus Greiner is the George Vasmer Leverett Professor of Physics at Harvard University, where he has been a faculty member since 2005. He is one of the principal architects of quantum gas microscopy — the technique that enables single-atom imaging and manipulation within optical lattices at the scale of individual lattice sites — and a pioneer of quantum simulation with ultracold atoms.

properties.name: Antoine Browaeys

current_position.institution: Institut d'Optique Graduate School / Laboratoire Charles Fabry, CNRS
current_position.title: Directeur de recherche (Research Director)

properties.short_bio: Antoine Browaeys is Directeur de recherche (Research Director) at the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS), based at the Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique Graduate School in Palaiseau, France. He is one of the world's foremost experimental physicists in the field of neutral atom quantum simulation and computing, pioneering the use of optical tweezer arrays loaded with individual Rydberg atoms.

properties.name: Thierry Lahaye

current_position.institution: Institut d'Optique Graduate School / Laboratoire Charles Fabry, CNRS
current_position.title: Directeur de recherche (Senior Researcher, DR2)

properties.short_bio: Thierry Lahaye is Directeur de recherche (Senior Researcher, DR2) at the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS), based at the Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique Graduate School in Palaiseau, France. He co-leads the "Quantum Optics – Atoms" group with Antoine Browaeys, where the team pioneers neutral-atom quantum simulation and computing using arrays of single Rydberg atoms in optical tweezers.

properties.name: Manuel Endres
properties.short_bio: Manuel Endres is Professor of Physics at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), where he has led the Endres Lab since 2015 (initially as Visiting Associate, promoted to Assistant Professor in 2016 and Full Professor in 2021). His group develops optical tweezer array platforms for quantum computing, quantum simulation, and precision metrology, with a particular focus on alkaline-earth (strontium) neutral atoms and Rydberg qubit control.

properties.name: Adam M. Kaufman

current_position.title: JILA Fellow and Associate Professor of Physics

properties.short_bio: Adam M. Kaufman is a JILA Fellow, NIST Physicist, and Associate Professor of Physics at the University of Colorado Boulder, where he leads the Kaufman Group at JILA. He joined JILA as an Associate Fellow and Assistant Professor Adjoint in July 2017 and was promoted to JILA Fellow and Associate Professor in March 2022.

properties.name: Jeff D. Thompson

current_position.title: Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering

properties.short_bio: Jeff D. Thompson is an Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Princeton University, where he joined the faculty as an Assistant Professor in February 2016 and was promoted to Associate Professor in January 2022. He is also affiliated with the Princeton Quantum Initiative.

properties.name: Hannes Bernien
properties.short_bio: Hannes Bernien is a Full Professor of Experimental Physics at the University of Innsbruck and Scientific Director at the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information (IQOQI) of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, positions he assumed in 2025. Prior to this, he was an Assistant Professor of Molecular Engineering at the University of Chicago's Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering (2019–2025).

properties.name: Christian Groß

current_position.title: W3 Professor of Experimental Many-Particle Quantum Physics

properties.short_bio: Christian Groß is W3 Professor of Experimental Many-Particle Quantum Physics at the University of Tübingen, where he has led the Quantum Many-Body Physics group since September 2019. He is one of the foremost experimentalists in quantum gas microscopy, having co-developed a world-leading platform using ultracold fermionic lithium atoms in optical lattices that enables single-atom and single-spin resolved imaging of strongly correlated quantum many-body systems.

current_position.title: Theodore William Richards Professor of Chemistry; Professor of Physics
Professor of Physics (Judith and Harold Rosenberg Chair in Quantum Computing)

current_position.institution: Centro de Investigación en Nanomateriales y Nanotecnología (CINN-CSIC)
current_position.title: Tenured Scientist

properties.name: Peter Zoller
properties.short_bio: Peter Zoller is a theoretical physicist and one of the founding figures of quantum information science. He is Emeritus Professor of Theoretical Physics at the University of Innsbruck and served as Scientific Director at the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information (IQOQI) of the Austrian Academy of Sciences from 2003 to 2024.

properties.name: Klaus Mølmer
properties.short_bio: Klaus Mølmer is a theoretical physicist and one of the founding figures of quantum optics and quantum information theory. He is Professor of Physics at the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, where he joined in 2022 after holding a full professorship at Aarhus University from 2000 to 2022.

properties.name: Hannes Pichler
properties.short_bio: Hannes Pichler is a theoretical physicist and Professor of Theoretical Physics at the University of Innsbruck, where he has held his chair since June 2020. He is also Research Director of the Pichler Group — Quantum Science Theory at the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information (IQOQI) of the Austrian Academy of Sciences in Innsbruck. He was born in 1986 in Brixen (South Tyrol, Italy).

current_position.title: Victor F. Weisskopf Assistant Professor of Physics

properties.name: Tommaso Calarco
properties.short_bio: Tommaso Calarco is Director of the Institute for Quantum Control (PGI-8) at Forschungszentrum Jülich, a position he has held since September 2018. He is concurrently Professor of Quantum Information at the University of Cologne and the University of Bologna. He is one of Europe's foremost figures in quantum technologies policy and quantum optimal control theory.

properties.name: Andrew J. Daley
properties.short_bio: Andrew J. Daley is Professor of Quantum Physics in the Atomic and Laser Physics sub-department at the University of Oxford, and Tutorial Fellow in Physics at Keble College. His research spans the boundary between quantum optics, many-body physics, and quantum technologies, focusing on non-equilibrium dynamics of ultracold quantum gases, open quantum systems, and tensor-network numerical methods.

properties.name: Thomas Pohl
properties.short_bio: Thomas Pohl is a Professor of Theoretical Physics at the Institute for Theoretical Physics at TU Wien (Vienna University of Technology), where he leads the Pohl Group focusing on many-body quantum optics and light-matter interactions. He previously held a Niels Bohr Professorship at Aarhus University (2017–2023) funded by the Danish National Research Foundation, and was a Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems in Dresden (2008–2017).

properties.name: Hans Peter Büchler
properties.short_bio: Hans Peter Büchler is Professor of Theoretical Physics at the Institute for Theoretical Physics III (ITP3) at the University of Stuttgart, where he has held the chair since 2007. He holds the degree Dr. sc. nat. (Doctor of Natural Sciences) from ETH Zürich (2003), where he worked under Gianni Blatter on phase transitions in quantum condensed matter. He then carried out postdoctoral research from 2004 to 2007 with Peter Zoller at the University of Innsbruck, which shaped his focus on cold-atom quantum simulation and Rydberg physics.

current_position.title: Professor of Theoretical Atomic Physics and Synthetic Quantum Systems

properties.name: Dieter Jaksch

current_position.title: Professor of Physics (Theory of Many-Body Quantum Optical Systems)

properties.short_bio: Dieter Jaksch is a theoretical physicist and Professor for Theory of Many-Body Quantum Optical Systems at the Institute for Quantum Physics, Universität Hamburg, which he joined in the winter semester of 2021/22. He was previously Professor of Physics at the University of Oxford (2010–2021), where he had been a faculty member since 2003.

properties.name: Guido Pupillo
properties.short_bio: Guido Pupillo is a Distinguished Professor at the Université de Strasbourg, where he directs the European Center for Quantum Sciences (CESQ) and the Quantum Physics Laboratory at ISIS. He is a leading theorist in the physics of Rydberg-dressed atoms and strongly correlated quantum many-body systems.

properties.name: Nir Bar-Gill
properties.short_bio: Prof. Nir Bar-Gill is a Full Professor jointly appointed in the Racah Institute of Physics and the Department of Applied Physics at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. He heads the Quantum Information, Simulation and Sensing (QISS) lab.

properties.name: Jiangfeng Du
properties.short_bio: Jiangfeng Du (born June 1969, Wuxi, Jiangsu) is a Chinese physicist and academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (elected 2015) who built one of the world's leading groups in spin-based quantum information and precision measurement using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond.

properties.name: Oliver Benson
properties.short_bio: Oliver Benson is Professor of Experimental Nano-Optics at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, where he has led the Nano Optics group at the Institute of Physics since 2001. His research spans quantum optics, single-photon sources, NV-center photonics in diamond, nano-optics, cavity QED, and quantum plasmonics.

properties.name: Machiel Blok

current_position.title: Assistant Professor of Physics and Astronomy

properties.short_bio: Machiel Blok is Assistant Professor of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Rochester, where he leads the Blok Lab. He completed his PhD at Delft University of Technology under Ronald Hanson, working on quantum measurement and real-time feedback with NV center spin registers in diamond. Following a postdoc in Irfan Siddiqi's group at UC Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Lab (2015–2019), he joined Rochester in 2020. His current research focuses on qudit quantum computing and quantum simulation with superconducting transmon circuits, pioneering the use of higher-dimensional (beyond qubit) encodings to improve quantum processor performance and error resilience.

properties.name: Robert Schoelkopf

current_position.title: Sterling Professor of Applied Physics and Physics; Director, Yale Quantum Institute

properties.short_bio: Robert Schoelkopf is Sterling Professor of Applied Physics and Physics at Yale University and Director of the Yale Quantum Institute. He co-founded circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED), co-invented the transmon qubit, and has led experimental demonstrations of quantum algorithms and error correction in superconducting integrated circuits.

properties.name: David Schuster

current_position.title: Joan Reinhart Professor of Applied Physics

properties.short_bio: David Schuster is the Joan Reinhart Professor of Applied Physics at Stanford University, where his group develops superconducting quantum circuits for quantum computing, simulation, and hybrid quantum systems. He previously held a faculty position at the University of Chicago (c. 2012–2022). He completed his PhD and postdoc in the Schoelkopf Lab at Yale, where he was first author on the landmark 2007 Nature paper resolving individual photon number states in a superconducting circuit. His Stanford group pursues fluxonium-based high-fidelity gates, cavity-array quantum simulation, millimeter-wave to optical transduction via cold atoms, electron-on-helium qubits, and quantum-enhanced dark matter detection.

properties.name: Barbara M. Terhal
properties.short_bio: Barbara M. Terhal is a Professor at QuTech, Delft University of Technology (Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science), where she leads the Terhal Group focused on quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computation theory.

properties.name: Alexandre Blais

current_position.title: Professeur titulaire (Full Professor), Département de physique; Scientific Director, Institut quantique

properties.short_bio: Alexandre Blais is Full Professor (Professeur titulaire) of Physics at Université de Sherbrooke and Scientific Director of the Institut quantique. He is the co-inventor of circuit quantum electrodynamics (circuit QED), the theoretical architecture — coupling superconducting qubits to microwave resonators — that underpins superconducting quantum processors at Google, IBM, and Amazon. He obtained his PhD at Sherbrooke (2002), did a postdoc with Girvin and Schoelkopf at Yale (2003–2005), then returned to Sherbrooke as faculty. He is a CIFAR Fellow (Quantum Information Science), Fellow of the American Physical Society, Member of the Royal Society of Canada, and has received the NSERC Steacie Fellowship (2010), Herzberg Medal (2011), Brockhouse Medal (2020), Rutherford Memorial Medal (2018), and Guggenheim Fellowship (2021).
